candidates.label: Recurrent right breast mastitis due to Streptococcus agalactiae infection, with hyperprolactinemia and milk stasis as contributing factors
Hyperprolactinemia with galactorrhea and recurrent mastitis, likely physiological postpartum pituitary hyperplasia
missing_or_uncertain: Prolactin level is high but postpartum

candidates.label: Prolactin-secreting pituitary microadenoma (occult) with hyperprolactinemia and recurrent mastitis
Inflammatory breast cancer of the right breast (rule out)
Chronic granulomatous mastitis of the right breast

response.rationale: The positive culture for Streptococcus agalactiae, leukocytosis, and breast erythema strongly support bacterial mastitis. The high prolactin and excessive milk production suggest hyperprolactinemia as a contributing factor, but the absence of a discrete pituitary mass on MRI makes a microadenoma less likely. Inflammatory breast cancer is unlikely given the infectious findings and lack of mass on ultrasound.
